summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute pyelonephritis and bilateral flank pain, consistent with his recurrent urinary tract infections. He has a history of T12 paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, ileal conduit, and chronic kidney disease. Imaging revealed moderate to severe left hydronephrosis, prompting a nephroureteral stent exchange on 2145-03-03. Urine cultures grew E. coli, Enterococcus, and Staph aureus, and due to multiple drug allergies, he was treated with IV tobramycin and daptomycin for two weeks. A midline was placed for antibiotic administration, as home infusion could not be arranged and the patient declined skilled nursing facility placement. During admission, he developed hyponatremia from excessive fluid intake, which resolved with fluid restriction. His kidney function remained within baseline, and the nephrostomy tube was recapped prior to discharge. He was discharged home with the nephrostomy tube in place, advised to follow up with urology within two weeks and to complete outpatient lab work to monitor renal and electrolyte status.
problems: Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
